_**Agent (auto-low)**_

Your notes garden is built for **two lanes**: understand ideas through linked reading, then **drill** the ones you need under pressure. Learning is not "read everything once."

## The guiding question

From your flashcards spec:

> **Can I recall and use this knowledge when it matters?**

Not card count, streak length, or how many notes you opened. The three outcomes are **retention**, **application**, and **explanation**.

---

## Lane 1: Read for understanding (the wiki)

Start from a hub, not random browsing:

| If you want… | Start here |
|---|---|
| How the garden works | [Getting Started](/notes/getting-started/) |
| PKM topics | [Maps of Content](/notes/maps-of-content/) |
| Faith / gospel | [Eternal Principles](/notes/eternal-principles/) → [Free Grace](/notes/free-grace/) first |
| Surprise connections | [Random Duo](/notes/random-duo/) |

### How to read one note (top to bottom)

Each atomic note is layered on purpose. On a page like [The Wise Builder](/notes/the-wise-builder/):

1. **`description`** — one-breath definition. Can you quote it cold?
2. **`key_concept`** — the real argument. Many notes use Level 1→5 depth; skim Level 1 first, go deeper only if you need nuance.
3. **`examples`** — two different scenes. Do they feel real? That's the "does this land?" check.
4. **Shareable thoughts** — four standalone one-liners. Good quick recall test.
5. **Relationships** — typed links (`extends`, `contradicts`). Follow these when you want context, not every wikilink at once.
6. **Flashcards** (bottom) — only on ~20% of spine notes with `review: true`.

Then use the graph around the note: **relationship neighbors**, **outgoing links**, **see also**, **backlinks**. Hover wikilinks for previews instead of opening every tab.

### Layered reading (don't one-pass it)

Your garden explicitly treats one read as insufficient ([Layered Reading](/notes/layered-reading/)):

```
Pass 1: description + shareable thoughts (gist)
Pass 2: key_concept + examples (understanding)
Pass 3: relationships + linked notes (context)
Pass 4: teach it back or use it this week (proof)
```

[Active Reading](/notes/active-reading/) applies the same idea to books: mark → extract → your own words, not yellow highlights that die in the margin.

---

## Lane 2: Drill for recall (flashcards)

The wiki holds nuance. Cards wire **life's cue → move** so the right default loads when the moment hits.

### On the note page

Notes with `review: true` (like The Wise Builder) show six scenario cards at the bottom. Flip them **from memory** before reading the back — don't re-read the note first.

### Review session

Go to [/notes/review/](/notes/review/):

- **Start review** — spaced repetition in the browser
- **Filter by `card_sets`** — e.g. `Eternal Principles`, `Gospel`, `Discipleship`, `Capture`, `Review`
- Rate yourself: Again / Hard / Good / Easy
- Progress saves **in this browser only**; use Anki export if you want phone sync

Card shape (from your spec):

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Front** | A moment that could happen this week (`"Bible study Monday, same gossip Tuesday"`) |
| **Back** | One immediate move (`"Do what he said - match hearing."`) |

**Litmus test:** Read only the front. Could this happen tomorrow? Cover the back — do you know what to **do** in the next five seconds?

---

## Lane 3: Maintain the garden (scheduled revisit)

Cards handle **timed drill**. The graph needs **calendar review**:

- [Periodic Knowledge Review](/notes/periodic-knowledge-review/) — weekly/quarterly passes, like bills on a calendar
- [Spaced Repetition](/notes/spaced-repetition/) — short reps on rhythm, not one Sunday marathon
- [Issues](/notes/issues/) — fix broken links during maintenance

Crisis review (only opening notes when something breaks) is explicitly the anti-pattern.

---

## A practical weekly rhythm

Something like this matches how the garden is designed:

| When | What |
|---|---|
| **Daily (5–10 min)** | [/notes/review/](/notes/review/) — drill due cards |
| **Weekly** | One hub section or MOC; [Random Duo](/notes/random-duo/) for connection prompts |
| **When stuck** | Follow `contradicts` / `extends` links from the note you're on |
| **Quarterly** | Walk [Issues](/notes/issues/), prune stale notes, promote fleeting → evergreen |

---

## What *not* to do

- Don't try to memorize every note — only ~20% have cards, and that's intentional ([Pareto](/notes/pareto-principle/) spine).
- Don't treat reading the wiki as studying — recognition while scrolling ≠ recall under pressure.
- Don't binge-review — `"Five cards today. Same time tomorrow."` is a card in the deck for a reason.

---

**Short version:** Read hubs → one note at a time (description → concept → examples → links) → drill spine cards at [/notes/review/](/notes/review/) → revisit the graph on a schedule. Success is acting correctly when life shows up, not finishing the garden.

If you want, I can sketch a **first-week path** through Eternal Principles or the PKM spine using only notes that already have review cards.

## Best home: a new atomic note

Create something like **`reading-the-garden.md`** (or `learn-from-notes.md`).

**One claim to anchor it:**

> Learn from the garden in two lanes — wiki for understanding, cards for drill.

That matches your atomic-note rule. The rest (field order, weekly rhythm, what not to do) becomes `key_concept` layers and body links, not a second note.

**Why a new note beats stuffing an existing one:**

| Option | Fit |
|--------|-----|
| **[Getting Started](/notes/getting-started/)** | Good for a *pointer*, not the full workflow. It's already about creating notes and site tools. |
| **[Flashcards](/notes/flashcards/)** / **[Review](/notes/review/)** | Meta tool pages — format and UI only. |
| **[Layered Reading](/notes/layered-reading/)** | Reading *external* sources in passes — related, different claim. |
| **[Spaced Repetition](/notes/spaced-repetition/)** | Already has wiki vs drill — link *from* the new note, don't duplicate. |
| **[The Second Brain Workflow](/notes/the-second-brain-workflow/)** | CODE/PARA loop — capture to express, not how to read notes. |

## How to wire it in

1. **New note** — frontmatter claim + layered `key_concept`; link to:
   - [Layered Reading](/notes/layered-reading/) — depth passes on a source
   - [Active Reading](/notes/active-reading/) — mark → extract
   - [Spaced Repetition](/notes/spaced-repetition/) — drill lane
   - [Periodic Knowledge Review](/notes/periodic-knowledge-review/) — calendar revisit
   - [Eternal Principles](/notes/eternal-principles/) — faith entry point
   - Tool URLs only: `/notes/review/`, `/notes/flashcards/` (no wikilinks to meta pages)

2. **[Getting Started](/notes/getting-started/)** — add a short body section, e.g. `## Learn from notes`, with one paragraph + link to the new note.

3. **[Maps of Content](/notes/maps-of-content/)** — under **Distill & review**, add the link next to Layered Reading and Periodic Knowledge Review.

4. **Optional `review: true`** — if you want cards for the workflow itself ("opened six tabs, no recall" → "description first, then review").

## What not to do

Don't put the full guide in **Getting Started** — it will bloat the onboarding hub. Don't put it in **flashcards.md** — that's author spec, not reader workflow.
